entries.name: Brad Beneke

expected.charges: Interfering with the Selective Service System (the July 1970 Minnesota draft-board raids).
expected.sentence: Verdict as recorded: Convicted; most sentenced to five years and released July 1973.

entries.rationale: MNHS chronology names Beneke among those sentenced December 28, 1970. This is sentencing only; do not equate with prison admission.

entries.name: Charles Muse

expected.charges: Selective Service violation arising from refusal to cooperate with military conscription
expected.sentence: Served a federal prison term at Allenwood and was released in December 1968. The original sentence and exact custody endpoints remain unresolved.

entries.rationale: Contemporary September 1969 report says Muse left Allenwood last December. Fill December 1968 month on the separate draft-refusal case, preserving Chicago Fifteen case. Day 1 is storage placeholder.

entries.name: Carlos Feliciano

expected.charges: Pretrial detention in the New York explosives prosecution
expected.sentence: Sixteen months of pretrial imprisonment reported by the archival finding aid; released on bail in 1972. A later conviction and prison term are recorded separately.

updates.sentence: Held in pretrial detention from May 16, 1970 until release on bail September 29, 1971. Contemporary reporting summarized this as sixteen months. A later conviction and prison term are recorded separately.

entries.rationale: Original September 17 page 16 explicitly held since May 16, 1970; October 15 page 2 explicitly physical bail release September 29, 1971. Both visually verified. Correct misleading 1972 endpoint and May 21 arrest; use exact interval instead of rounded sixteen months. Later 1973 case untouched.

entries.name: Carter Camp

expected.charges: Assault on a United States Marshal at Wounded Knee
expected.sentence:
3 years imposed; conviction later reversed on appeal (1976). Accounts of time actually served at Leavenworth vary (obituaries cite roughly two to three years).

Verdict as recorded: Convicted 1975 (Cedar Rapids), but the conviction was reversed on appeal in 1976 — United States v. Camp, 541 F.2d 737 (8th Cir.) — for a defective indictment
